title: From Plaque Disclosure to Real-Time, At-Home Feedback: How AI Is Changing Patient Coaching in Dentistry
html:
Written by: Sarah Balaster, DMD

As clinicians, we are trained to recognize findings that patients often cannot see for themselves, from plaque and biofilm accumulation to inflammation, bone loss, demineralization, and disease progression. Helping patients understand those findings has always been essential because people are far more likely to change behavior when they can visualize the problem.

For generations, some of our most effective patient education tools have shared a common purpose: making the invisible visible.

Artificial intelligence is helping bridge that gap.  AI-assisted platforms such as Overjet translate radiographic findings into color coded visual overlays that help patients better understand demineralization, bone loss, and other treatment concerns. By making these findings easier to visualize, AI is creating a common language between clinician and patient.

For many practices, AI has transformed patient education by making complex radiographic findings easier to understand. The technology is impressive, but the experience still takes place during a dental visit.

Long before AI-assisted radiographs, dentists used plaque-disclosing solutions to make the invisible visible to patients. Patients who believe they are brushing effectively can instantly see areas of retained biofilm that might otherwise go unnoticed. Two-tone systems further enhanced the educational experience by differentiating newer plaque from mature plaque.

Like AI-enhanced radiographs, plaque disclosure helps patients visualize a problem they might otherwise miss and encourages meaningful behavior change. While these teaching moments occur primarily in the operatory, home is where oral health decisions are made every day. AI is now beginning to provide guidance there as well.

The Philips Sonicare Next-Generation DiamondClean Prestige 9900 represents a new application of AI in patient education. Features such as Smart Coverage Feedback and the on-device Mouth Map, displayed directly on the toothbrush handle, provide information about brushing coverage and any missed areas, bringing visual feedback into the home environment. The AI technology was trained using data from nearly 20,000 brushing sessions and integrates information from sensors embedded within the toothbrush handle to predict brush location and monitor brushing pressure. During brushing, the handle can automatically reduce intensity when excessive pressure is detected.

One of the most compelling aspects of this technology is the Mouth Map feature. After each brushing session, the display presents a 12-segment mouth map, highlighting the amount of time spent brushing each segment. By tracking brushing coverage, it helps patients identify areas that may have been missed or received less brushing time during their oral hygiene routine. The same educational principle of making the invisible visible that make radiographs and plaque-disclosing agents effective are now being applied during daily home care.

The system also addresses another common challenge in oral hygiene instruction: brushing pressure. Many patients are unaware that they brush too aggressively until recession, abrasion, or tissue trauma becomes clinically evident. SenseIQ technology automatically adjusts brushing intensity and provides feedback when excessive pressure is detected helping patients correct the habit as it occurs rather than months later at a recall visit.

From AI-enhanced radiographs and plaque-disclosing solutions to real-time brushing feedback technologies, patient coaching continues to evolve beyond the walls of the dental office. Patients can now receive guidance not only during clinical visits but also during the daily habits that influence oral health outcomes.

As AI technologies continue to advance, their ability to deliver meaningful feedback in real time may help patients better understand their oral health, reinforce positive behaviors, and take a more active role in their care.
